quickfire.question: Which field is required in every singly linked list node declaration?
options: A pointer to the previous node
A pointer to the next node
quickfire.answer: A pointer to the next node

routineWriter.questionText: Write the node declaration (struct) for a singly linked list in C.

commonMistakes.description: next must be a pointer to struct Node — a value type creates infinite recursion
The data field — omitting it is incomplete

quickfire.question: In insertAtEnd, the while-loop condition that walks to the last node is: while (curr->next _____ NULL)

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for insertAtEnd in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Empty-list guard — missing this causes a null-dereference on the traversal
Stop at last node (curr->next is NULL), not at NULL itself
Attach new node — using curr = newNode instead leaves the list unchanged

fullTrace.questionText: Show the step-by-step state after inserting 10, 20, 30 into an initially empty singly linked list.

quickfire.question: When deleting a node from a singly linked list, which pointer must be updated?

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for delete (by value) in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Head-node special case — deleting head requires updating *head itself
Bypass the deleted node by pointing predecessor to successor
Must free — omitting causes a memory leak

quickfire.question: What is the time complexity of finding the k-th node in a singly linked list?

routineWriter.questionText: Write a routine to traverse and print every value in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Use a separate pointer — never mutate head during traversal
Loop terminates when curr is NULL, not curr->next
